seoTitle: JavaScript Minifier - Compress JS Code Online
metaDescription: Free online JavaScript Minifier. Compress JS code to reduce file size, improve website load times, and obfuscate your scripts. Fast and secure.
intro: Is JavaScript dragging down your PageSpeed score? Our free JS Minifier instantly compresses your scripts, ensuring your interactive web applications load as fast as possible.
whatIs: The JavaScript Minifier is a crucial optimization tool that reduces the byte size of JS files. It safely removes formatting, comments, and dead spaces to accelerate script downloading and browser execution.
howToUse: Paste your working, uncompressed JavaScript code into the tool.
The tool processes the code and outputs a dense, compressed block.
Copy the code to your `script.min.js` file.
howItWorks: The tool uses a syntax parser to safely remove single-line `//` and multi-line `/* */` comments. It deletes line breaks and trims unnecessary spaces around mathematical operators and variable assignments without altering the logic.
resultInterpretation: Your logic functions exactly the same, but the browser has to download significantly fewer bytes. The code is also much harder for casual users to read (a process known as obfuscation).
useCases: Web App Deployment: Compressing custom scripts before launching a React or Vue application.
Ad Tech & Tracking: Ensuring third-party analytics pixels are as small as possible so they don't slow down client websites.
Bandwidth Savings: Reducing server costs on highly-trafficked websites by serving smaller asset files.
tipsAndLimitations: Make sure your JavaScript is free of syntax errors before minifying. A missing semicolon in uncompressed code can sometimes cause minified code to break.
This tool performs basic minification (removing spaces/comments) but does not perform advanced 'uglification' (like renaming long variable names to single letters).

faq.question: What is the difference between minification and obfuscation?
faq.answer: Minification just removes spaces and comments to save space. Obfuscation deliberately scrambles variable names to make the code impossible for humans to reverse-engineer. Minification naturally causes a light level of obfuscation.

faq.question: Will minifying JavaScript break my website?
faq.answer: It shouldn't, as long as your original code is syntactically correct. However, always test your `.min.js` file thoroughly before deploying to production.

disclaimer: Tool performs local, regex-based minification. It relies on standard ASI (Automatic Semicolon Insertion) rules; poorly formatted original JS may experience issues.
